meta.title: How Time Flies By
meta.footerNote: Beat outline · bullets to hit, not final VO

sections.label: Cold Open
sections.sublabel: Drop into the moment the tweet finally landed

items.text: Talk about the moment the tweet landed. What time of day, where were you sitting, what was around you? [PLACEHOLDER — city, room, chair]
Read the Hormozi tweet out loud, word for word: "Once you realize just how much more work it takes to go from good to great…you realize you can only be great at a few things and ignore the rest."
This wasn't the first time you read it. What number read was it? Why did THIS one hit when the others didn't? [PLACEHOLDER]
Pivot line: "I'd read this tweet a dozen times. This was the first time it meant something."

musicCue.title: [TBD]
musicCue.desc: Quiet, suspended. Don't compete with the tweet read. Single sustained note under the pivot line.

shotList.desc: Open mid-scroll on phone or laptop. The actual tweet on the actual scroll. No intro, no logo, no "hey everyone."
Full-screen tweet text overlay during the verbatim read.
Cut to face on the pivot line. Quiet, not performed.

sections.label: Promise
sections.sublabel: Name the viewer and the deal

items.text: Who is this video for? Two candidates — pick one: (a) employed-and-comfortable past version of you, (b) anyone in their 20s who thinks they have time. [DECIDE]
State the deal: by the end, the viewer should see why the years they think they have are already half-spent.

Don't list takeaways. Make one promise, one sentence: "By the end I'm going to show you the math that broke me — and why if you're employed right now, you're sitting on the only window you'll ever have."

musicCue.title: (carries over from Cold Open)
musicCue.desc: No transition. Light build cued for pivot into The Break.

shotList.desc: Direct camera, slightly tighter framing. No B-roll yet — viewer should be locked on the face.

sections.label: The Break
sections.sublabel: The belief that broke: "I had time."

items.text: Confess the belief out loud, full sentence: "For five years I thought I was good, and I thought that was enough."

Why did it make sense? Walk through the evidence you had at the time: two jobs, two incomes, living abroad, taxes optimized, savings climbing. Say the numbers if you're willing. [PLACEHOLDER — pick which numbers go on camera]

What was the warning sign you kept ignoring? Was there ONE moment — a friend's comment, a recruiter message, an itch on a Sunday — where you knew the second skill was missing? [PLACEHOLDER — find the moment]
Don't resolve it yet. End on: "I didn't feel lazy. I felt earned. That was the trap."

musicCue.title: [TBD]
musicCue.desc: Push forward subtly. Tension building, not yet released.

shotList.desc: Direct address. This is the confession — eyes locked, no cuts away during the belief statement.
Optional: pull-quote overlay on the closing line.

sections.label: Scene 1
sections.sublabel: The Peak — when you thought you'd made it

items.text: Pick the specific month and place where the peak was. [PLACEHOLDER — what city, what month, what year]
Open with a sensory detail of comfort: morning routine, evening rhythm, the texture of your weekday. What did "comfortable" actually feel like in your body?
Name the high school dream out loud: money on the internet, travel, retire early. Then say: "And I had done all three."
Drop in the numbers, if you'll say them: two incomes for one person's hours, tax savings, monthly burn. [PLACEHOLDER — decide what's on camera]
BUT — one foreshadowing beat. Was there a moment in the peak where something didn't sit right? Even small. A Sunday feeling. A quiet question. [PLACEHOLDER]

musicCue.title: [TBD]
musicCue.desc: Warm, slightly nostalgic. The good times — but a small unease underneath.

shotList.desc: [TBD] — old footage / photos from the abroad period if you have any. If not, recreate the routine.
Mix with B-roll. Voice over the visual.
Numbers on screen if you'll show them: salary, savings rate, hours/week.

items.text: First firing — talk about the moment. Where were you? What time of day? Who told you? What did you do in the next hour? [PLACEHOLDER]
Describe what happened, what you felt, what you did. Don't editorialize from the present — be there.
Second firing. How long after the first? Did you see it coming or did it ambush you? [PLACEHOLDER]
First morning waking up with no jobs at all — what was the first thought? One real sentence.
Land the scene on: "For the first time in five years, nobody needed me at a computer."

musicCue.title: [TBD]
musicCue.desc: Drop. Something sparse, hollow. Don't make it sad — make it quiet.

shotList.desc: Close framing for the firings. Let the viewer sit with you.
[TBD] — desk, empty calendar, the apartment in the morning.

sections.label: Scene 3
sections.sublabel: Starting Over — the math is brutal

items.text: When did the YouTube decision happen? Was it a clear moment or a slow drift? [PLACEHOLDER — find the day or the week]
Be honest about what you thought it would take. Three months? Six? A year? Say the wrong number out loud — viewers connect to it more than the right one.
BUT — first reality check. What was the first thing that took 10x longer than expected? Editing? Writing? Thumbnails? The first script? [PLACEHOLDER — pick the one that hit you hardest]

Layer in the fear questions but DON'T resolve them: will the savings last? Will you have to go back to the US? Manual labor? Will anyone even hire you with AI eating the market? Say them out loud once, then move on.

musicCue.title: [TBD]
musicCue.desc: Working music — but anxious, not hopeful.

shotList.desc: [TBD] — your actual editing timeline, Notion, blank doc, whatever the start-over looked like.
Direct on the fear questions. One sentence each, no list framing.

sections.label: Scene 4
sections.sublabel: The Tweet Lands — return to the cold open

items.text: Return to the cold open moment. Now the viewer has the context — walk through what shifted in your head between then and now.
Read the tweet again. Walk through the math out loud: ten years to good at code, five years coasted, how many years to good at THIS new thing? [PLACEHOLDER — say the honest number]
What did you do for the rest of that day after it hit? Did you tell anyone? Did you write anything down? Did you keep scrolling? [PLACEHOLDER — the unglamorous answer is the better one]
Land the scene on: "I wasn't sad I got fired. I was sad about the five years before that."

musicCue.title: [TBD]
musicCue.desc: Mirror the Cold Open music. Same texture, now with weight under it.

shotList.desc: Return to the same chair, same scroll. Visual symmetry with Cold Open.
Re-show the tweet with on-screen math: years to good, years to great, years coasted.
Locked face on the closing line. No cuts.

sections.label: Scene 5
sections.sublabel: The Animation Math — three hours, four seconds

items.text: Three hours of work. Four seconds of output. Say the ratio out loud.
Project the math forward on camera: at this rate, X hours = Y minutes of finished video = Z videos a year. Run the actual numbers, don't sanitize. [PLACEHOLDER]
Ask the question and don't answer it: "Does the math close before the savings run out?"
Let the silence sit. This is the lowest point of the video — don't rescue it.

musicCue.title: [TBD]
musicCue.desc: Sparse to silent. Let the math do the work. Drop the music entirely on the unanswered question.

shotList.desc: Open on the actual animation editor — Premiere / After Effects / whatever. Real timeline, real timestamp visible.
On-screen math: hours / output / projected runway. Numbers do the talking.
Cut to face on the unanswered question. Hold. Don't blink past it.

sections.label: The Lesson
sections.sublabel: Close the loop, crystallize, leave them with one move

items.text: Close the loop — bring the viewer back to the cold open moment one final time.
I didn't lose my job. I lost five years I could've spent becoming great at something else — and I gave them away to be comfortable.
Generalize for the viewer in ONE sentence: comfort is the most expensive thing you'll ever buy with your time, and you only notice the bill when the comfort is gone.

Hand the viewer ONE specific action — something they can do tonight. Suggested: "If you're employed and comfortable right now, pick one skill you'd want to be great at in five years and put one hour into it before you go to bed."

musicCue.title: [TBD]
musicCue.desc: Bring the Cold Open music back, fuller now. Resolution, not relief.
musicCue.note: Cut music two beats before the action prompt. Last line should be dry.

shotList.desc: Visual return to Cold Open — same chair, same scroll. Symmetry closes the story.
Locked face for the crystallized line. No cuts. No movement.
Pull-quote overlay on the crystallized line — large, screenshotable.
Action prompt direct to camera. Slight forward lean if you want.
NO like/sub before the lesson lands. Like/sub end-card goes AFTER the action prompt.
